brief: The Market Ear argues tech is trapped at resistance but the setup underneath is skewed bullish, so the pain trade is higher. GS's case: S&P 500 EPS grew roughly 30% year-on-year in Q2 while sentiment stays bearish, NDX shorts rose 35% since June, long/short net leverage sits in the 6th percentile, gross tech exposure in the 43rd percentile, and cash balances hold at $163 billion. GS's Flood, back from Asia, found caution dominating as July's crash left scar tissue (some funds gave back over 20% of YTD gains) and geopolitics, rates and inflation muted risk appetite, and he sees the IPO pipeline as a potential catalyst. BofA notes long-end yields hit multi-year highs on fiscal concerns, but calls the shock far milder than 2022 (30-year drawdown around 7% versus 25%, S&P around 9% versus 25%) and cites the dot-com era, when Nasdaq rallied despite rising rates. Nomura flags a large AI options buyer spending $315 million, reviving the spot-up, vol-up dynamic. If NDX breaks its resistance near the 100-day average, positioning and seasonality could turn it into a chase.
